title: Concept-based Steering of Large Language Models for Conditional Molecular Generation
experiments_summary: The experiments evaluate the proposed CAST framework across in-distribution and out-of-distribution (OOD) settings using multiple models and datasets. Specifically: (1) In-distribution evaluation uses the TDC molecular generation benchmark composed of ZINC, MOSES, and ChEMBL datasets; QED and LogP property values are computed via RDKit; 2000 randomly sampled property combinations per dataset are used; CAST is evaluated on Chemlactica-125M, Chemlactica-1.3B, Chemma-2B (steered at layers 6, 12, and 9 respectively), and Qwen3-4B (steered at layer 18); baselines include the vanilla base model, full SFT, LoRA fine-tuning, and the ActAdd activation steering method. (2) OOD evaluation follows the setup from Jolicoeur-Martineau et al. [2024] targeting specific single and combined out-of-distribution property values; the Conjugated-xTB dataset is also used, sampling 100 property combinations with 100 candidate molecules each. (3) Quantitative metrics used include MAE and Best100MAE for property alignment, Validity for chemical correctness, and Generative Efficiency (GenEff) for OOD novelty/uniqueness/validity. (4) Qualitative studies assess novelty (via PubChem membership) and synthesizability (via RDKit SA score) for both in-distribution and OOD settings. (5) Steering strength ablations are performed in two settings: Setting 1 varies the concept value c_j for one property at a time in [0,1] increments of 0.1, measuring min/max MAE across samples on the ZINC dataset; Setting 2 varies a global scalar multiplier alpha in [-2, 4] applied to the aggregated steering vector, measuring GenEff and Best100MAE in the OOD high-target setting. (6) The CBM and property predictor modules (two-layer MLPs with 4d and 2d intermediate dimensions) are trained using AdamW with early stopping on a single NVIDIA A100 40GB GPU, with LLM parameters kept frozen throughout.
